name: Webflow
look: Two-colour conversion hierarchy with a five-stop chromatic category palette used only as full card fills, and tight 4px buttons.

hero.title: The site your marketing team can actually edit
hero.sub: Design visually, publish real HTML and CSS, and hand editing to the people who write the copy without giving them the codebase.

features.title: Design, content and hosting
features.sub: The three things a marketing site needs, without three vendors and a handover between them.

items.title: Visual canvas
items.body: A real box model, not a page builder. What you build maps to the CSS that ships.

items.title: CMS
items.body: Collections with typed fields and reference relationships, editable by non-developers.

items.title: On-page editing
items.body: Editors change copy on the live page, in place, without touching structure.

items.title: Hosting included
items.body: Global CDN, automatic SSL and one-click publishing with rollback.

items.title: Clean export
items.body: Export the HTML, CSS and assets whenever you like. There is no proprietary runtime.

items.title: Roles
items.body: Designers build, editors edit, and the two cannot break each other's work.

showcases.title: Marketing stops queueing
showcases.body: Copy changes become copy changes rather than engineering tickets. The design system stays locked down while the words stay editable, which is the split every marketing site actually needs.

showcases.title: Governed at scale
showcases.body: Multiple sites under one workspace, with shared components, SSO, page-level permissions and an audit trail of who published what.

gallery.title: RESOURCES
gallery.sub: Templates, courses and the component marketplace.

notes: The conversion hierarchy is two colours: near-black for every primary CTA, white-on-hairline for every secondary. Chromatic accents never become button backgrounds.
The signature is a five-stop category palette — purple, pink, blue, orange, green — used at full saturation as card fills, each tied to a product surface.
Hero type is restrained: around 80px at weight 600 with slight negative tracking. Confident rather than billboard-loud.
One variable family covers display and body; a mono appears only on technical captions.
Buttons stay tight at 4px and cards at 8px. The brand never uses pill CTAs, and layered multi-offset shadows are its only elevation cue.
